Tygerberg Caravans

By: Liz Fish | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Caravans and camping is a huge industry in South Africa and once again it’s been hit by a fraudster – the son in law of a very reputable business, established in 1994, the GO TO place for camping Tygerberg Caravans. It’s been hollowed out from under their noses, Wesley Dempster swindled R20 million worth of caravans from 83 victims so far, and the numbers keep growing.

Summary:
This is how it goes. The original owner, Ben Barbour went into semi-retirement and his daughter and son in law and Westly Dempster ran the business. Westly started selling caravans for cash and putting the money into a private FNB account. He would sell consignment caravans and not pay the seller. Then sell it on, take the cash and sometimes deliver the caravan, sometimes not. He would sell the caravan and even deliver the vehicle promising the registration papers will follow, they never did.
Carl Fitchen, was told his caravan was sold for R225 000 and Wesley collected the papers promising Carl he would receive the money in 7 days, that turned to 10 days and the answers kept changing. Finally after weeks of back and forth Carl went into the dealership and was told Wesley had been suspended and they could give him no clear answers, and the owner was nowhere to be found. Carl turned to Facebook outing Tygerberg Caravans and Wesley and things began to explode. Within a week there were over 80 victims on the whatsapp group and it all came tumbling down.
There were victims on both ends of the deal. Elzette is a private investigator who can tell us all the different scams he got up to and is willing to do an on camera interview. People who had sold their caravans and not got their money and people who had bought caravans have not got the registration papers. Who does the vehicle belong to? The banks are financing the same caravan, not knowing that it’s owned by two different people. Some banks didn’t get the original Natis papers 7 months later and who does the caravan belong to? People have been handing in their caravans to be repaired and Wesley sold them. Westly was changing Vin numbers, taking registration papers from one caravan and attaching them to the wrong caravan.


Further information:
Some of the stories are heart breaking, one old couple live in their caravan and sold it to get an upgrade, now they homeless. Another have been living in the caravan for 6 weeks waiting for the papers to be delivered and the sheriff of the court arrived on the weekend and repossessed the vehicle and now they living in their sons tiny home. Another mother of 5 had been living in the caravan but returned it to be repaired and now is R450 000 out of pocket and at the end of the month will have nowhere to live. Caravans are luxury vehicles for many but for many others they have become their permanent homes.
Francois the former salesman says Westly told him he was going to take the business to a new level, all cash sales were going into a new FNB account and bank financed vehicles into the Tygerberg account. Francois is prepared to give us an interview. There are civil cases between the original owners and the new owners who are both out of pocket. We have no shortage of case studies , we have Ben Barbour and Wesley Dempster’s phone numbers and have both their business and home addresses so we can confront them.


Extra Budget Items:
Some case studies are in Gansbaai and Fisherhaven so I will need extra for the fuel costs, can Use my vehicle but mileage will be high

Script:


LINK: Caravanning is a great South African tradition which has been booming in recent years. People book their campsite years in advance and meet people from across the country, and of course compare caravans and equipment.
VO: Around Cape Town, Tygerberg Caravans has been a top seller for these vans and they go for anything up to a million rand.

Link: You can see there established 1994 a solid reputation with all its customers and many felt they knew the owner Ben Barber and his son in law Wesley Dempster as friends - almost family
Wayne: Wesley is a very charming individual and a nice guy
Script: From 2020 Wesley ran things on behalf of his father in law. Francois De Bryun was their top salesman and business boomed after the pandemic.
Francois Close to your summer months, you know, with school holidays. Then that went well selling caravans, anything between 15 to 20 on a good month.
Script: And Wesley could sell ice to an Eskimo.
Upsound Voice Note R140 this one is going for R149, …..I am sure we can work on the pricing there
Francois. We were told Wesley the sales manager is basically taking over. Of course, nobody questioned because he's the son in law of the owner. And we did what we were told. So basically say cash deals in this account and then your normal financial deals in the normal account, which was ABSA. So it was FNB an ABSA account.
Script: Two bank accounts for a business isn’t unusual, but apparently the owner wasn’t aware of it and Wesley was diverting millions of rands into the 2nd account. Wesley strung everyone along, selling caravans without their knowledge and not paying them out .
Derek: Edwin, this wasn't just your caravan.
Edwin: It was our home
Script: Edwin Harvey took early retirement to travel the country with his wife. They lived in their much-loved caravan for a year.. and when it needed repairs, he took it to the place he trusted: Tygerberg Caravans. In the meantime, they booked a room.
Edwin: When we went back to go collect some of the personal belongings. We discovered the caravan was not there anymore
Script: Wesley had sold their caravan without telling them… or agreeing a price!
Edwin I asked him, what did you sell my caravan for? And he kept on avoiding the amount he sold it for.
BREATHER
Script: Before long, Wesley began driving around in flashy new cars.
Wayne: I think it was an F type JAG ML65 AMG and A and his wife was driving and I think it was an XJ 6 …. He said it was his uncle that had emigrated and he was able to look after it.
BREATHER
Script: All it took was one unhappy customer to tug at the proverbial thread …and whole yarn unravelled.
Derek “ and now we going to meet the man who blew the lid on this whole saga
Script: Carl Fitschen was owed R225 000 after Wesley sold his caravan…and he wasn’t paying up, so Carl got his lawyer involved.
Carl: He phoned me the next morning and said, I've got very bad news for you and Wesley has been dismissed because there's fraud involved. He then got in touch I think the following day and said, Carl, I'm very sorry to tell you, but they've filed for voluntary liquidation.

Script: News travelled like wildfire - and an avalanche of caravaners responded

Carl: I posted on a few campsites my story, I realized I could not be the only one in this situation

LINK: After Carl blew the scam apart on Facebook he set up a WhatsApp group, pretty soon there were about 80 people supporting each other, and trying to unravel the mess and the extent of the fraud began to be revealed.
Script: Wesley and Ben Barber stopped answering their phones - and locked the gates, trapping people’s caravans inside - weeks went by without answers.
Edwin: - I've sort of basically accepted that I've lost 500,000. But for the wife coming out of the depression when I retired, this hits you boom downhill and it just spirals down again And she you wake up at, night and you lying next to her and she's crying

Derek: But how does it leave you and Helize with your retirement plans?

Edwin Ruined, ruined

BREATHER

Script: Unbeknown to his customers, Wesley was juggling caravans that didn't belong to him. This is how he did it: He allegedly forged signatures on change of ownership documents, and photographed registration papers, instead of having the original or natis documents. Then he transferred them into Tygerberg Caravans’ name…illegally. But what bamboozled people was how vehicle identification plates - or VIN numbers - were swapped around.

LINK The Vin number is the identifying signature of any vehicle, and the vin plates were just ripped off most of these caravans but underneath here if you join me it should be engraved on the chassis, but you can see it's just been ground off, so in many cases these Vin numbers were just changed to match other registration papers. So now who knows who owns that caravan.
Script: Wayne McKensie retrieved his van just before the gates were locked. It had been in for repairs and when he got home, he saw the vin plates gone, and the spare tyre swapped out for an old one…and that while Wayne was still paying off the bank!
Derek: So what does the bank say?
Wayne - When Tygerberg Caravans went into liquidation I phoned them for the natis and they phoned me back about an hour later asking me if I had it.

Script: The bank never managed to get the original documents from Wesley.

Wayne 23 06 50…. So I've been paying monthly on something that I don't own, the bank doesn't own.

Script: With the vin plate removed… what was Wesley up to?
Derek: Vin numbers of being ripped off the re engraved. Didn't you see any of that?
Francois: Wesley was doing something…, I said, What are you doing here boss He said, You don't need to know. That's when I turned around and walked away.
DRONE SHOT Breather

Link 21:50:46:18 we've arrived at Tygerberg caravans, and, uh. Yeah, it's an absolute circus. This wasn't arranged. These people are looking for their caravans or to see who now owns them

Derek “Pierre have you got a different story’
Pierre: eventually when the bubble burst here , I checked the VIN number on the, on the caravan itself, on the chassis. It didn't correspond to the legal documents that I have in my position. I've got paperwork saying I've got a caravan, but it's not in my yard. Laughing

Script: The WhatsApp group has become a support base of people trying to make sense of the fraud and their losses.. like newly divorced Olivia Sadie, a mother of 5 young children.

Derek: Olivia, so near and yet so far.
Olivia: I'm so glad it's still here. This was going to be the start of my new life with my kids, this is their school fees. I really needed this money. There's been times when my nervous system where I've just been shaking because this is this is all the money I have. You know, you left and it's standing half a meter away and I can't get to it.

Script: It all came to a head in August when Ben Barber discovered the second bank account. He fired Wesley and filed for voluntary liquidation. Wesley hastily tried covering his tracks

Francois: He sends me a WhatsApp and he says, listen Faff delete everything from your PC to do with FNB, delete everything off your phone. Which I didn't
LINK “The police say they are investigating 39 cases of fraud and theft amounting to R23 million and
Derek: Do you think Wesley was the mastermind?
Edwin: I find it extremely difficult that the owners of the business, Ben Barber and his daughters that work in the office above the shop overlooking the sales department, and watch Caravans go in and out all the time,, and not see it on their books doesn't make sense to me

Script: Wesley Dempster's lawyers say he won't be providing a statement and police are investigating. Ben Barber said his family is traumatised and declined an interview. Francois is the only one left answering the phone.

Derek: Looking back, do you think you may have been naive?
Francois: I think so. I sort of I don't know, it's because my mind, like I say I try to do my job and I didn't think much of it until it was until it all came out. And this is actually bigger than what I thought.

Script: Francois fears for his safety as Wesley and some customers have threatened him…with a wife and 3 children to support, he’s anxious to clear his name.

Francois: My best thing is try it. Sorry, I'm emotional. To help the clients that bought from us or Tygerberg caravans, just to get everything the way it was.

Breath
Script: Mobile retirement homes, life-savings and holiday dreams … stolen.
Carl’s case against the new owner of his van is yet to go to court..the liquidators released Olivia’s caravan…but the rest wait for the police…. .Campsites are booked - but who gets to take the caravan this December, when so many different people own the same van?
